headline: Apple extends free iPhone satellite access for another year
summary: Apple is extending free access to its satellite features for existing iPhone users for another year. This was revealed in a footnote to its iPhone 18 Pro press release.
details: Apple has officially extended free access to its Emergency SOS via Satellite feature for existing iPhone users for an additional year. This extension was quietly announced in a footnote within a press release for the new iPhone 18 Pro.

The feature, which allows users to connect to emergency services via satellite when outside cellular and Wi-Fi coverage, was initially offered for two years free with the purchase of an iPhone 14 or later. This move provides continued peace of mind for users in remote areas.

headline: Google will buy half the electricity from one of Finland's nuclear power plants
summary: Google is making a record €13bn investment in Finland's AI infrastructure, funding three new data centers and expanding an existing one. This deal includes a 22-year contract to power its growing AI services.
details: Google announced a record €13bn investment in Finland's AI infrastructure, which includes a 22-year contract with Fortum to buy up to 50% of the electricity from the Loviisa nuclear power plant. This massive package aims to power the growing demand for AI services.

This represents Google's largest single investment in Europe. The funds will establish three new data centers in Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala, and expand its existing facility in Hamina, which was originally converted from a paper mill in 2009.

The new infrastructure is crucial for supporting Google's AI products like its Gemini chatbot, alongside core services such as Search, Maps, and YouTube. The global AI boom is driving an unprecedented demand for vast networks of data centers.

Finland has become an attractive location for data centers due to its cool climate, abundant low-carbon electricity, and uncongested power grid. The naturally colder temperatures significantly reduce the energy required for cooling server-packed facilities.

Google projects that this investment will support over 37,000 jobs during the construction phases, which are scheduled for 2027 and 2028. It is also expected to boost Finland's GDP by an estimated €3.6bn annually.

The agreement with Fortum provides long-term financial stability for the Loviisa plant, which currently generates about 10% of Finland's electricity. This commitment will support an investment program aimed at extending the nuclear station's operational life and increasing its generating capacity.
